_about: TIA archive catalogue. kind=hosted: the full text is on this site (content/texts/<id>.txt, public domain in the US and in life+70 countries). A hosted work with rights=cc-by-sa is a public-domain original in a translation made for the Marxists Internet Archive, which licenses its volunteers' work CC BY-SA; give the translator and source URL in edition and in the text. kind=link: the work is still under copyright here or not yet transcribed, so we point to where it is legally hosted. key=true puts the work on the author's card. cols lists the collections a work belongs to. Run tools/build_archive.py after editing.

collections.title: THE PROGRAMME
collections.desc: The communist programme as it was first written down and then defended against every revision: the Manifesto, the critique of Gotha, the Erfurt commentary, The State and Revolution and the theses of the Communist Left. Read in order, they state one programme.

collections.title: MARX AND ENGELS
collections.desc: The work of the two founders, from Engels's study of Manchester to the last prefaces he wrote in London.

collections.title: SECOND INTERNATIONAL
collections.desc: The mass parties of the Second International, their theory and the arguments that split them, ending with the collapse of August 1914.

collections.title: LENIN AND OCTOBER
collections.desc: The Bolshevik party, the revolutions of 1905 and 1917, and the first years of the Soviet republic, in the words of the people who led them.

collections.title: THE GERMAN LEFT
collections.desc: Rosa Luxemburg against revisionism, against the party bureaucracy and against the war, up to the Spartacus uprising.

collections.title: THE COMMUNIST LEFT
collections.desc: The Italian Communist Left: the founding theses of the Communist Party of Italy, the fight inside the Communist International and the post-war work of restoring the programme.

collections.title: BEYOND EUROPE
collections.desc: Marxism in Asia, Africa and the Americas.
